limits.effect: Excess rejects the specimen before worker launch: bad_request with host-owned admission_failure.
limits.behavior: At-limit, over-limit and multibyte admission controls through the CLI.

limits.title: Worker readiness hint wait
limits.counting: Initial ready-byte polling budget.
limits.effect: Expiry alone does not abort: the host still checks shared-memory publication.
limits.control: Production default; test-only controls are not a public tuning interface.
limits.behavior: Normal readiness is tested; expiry without aborting is source-inspected.

limits.title: Worker publication wait
limits.counting: Nominal polling budget for worker sentinels. Synchronous validator work is outside this budget.
limits.effect: Expiry can trigger worker cleanup and runner_timeout with partial evidence.
limits.control: Production default; test-only controls are not a public tuning interface.
limits.behavior: Deadline and partial-publication paths use shortened test budgets; the production duration is source-inspected.

limits.title: Worker exit grace
limits.counting: Polling grace after the host requests exit.
limits.effect: Expiry triggers a SIGKILL attempt, then reaping. Kill/reap failures remain reported.
limits.control: Production default; test-only controls are not a public tuning interface.
limits.behavior: Deadline/cleanup paths use controlled children; the production duration is source-inspected.

limits.title: Validator I/O deadline
limits.counting: Elapsed deadline for nonblocking probe writes and verdict reads.
limits.effect: Retains received verdicts and records an I/O timeout; cleanup follows.
limits.control: Production default; test-only controls are not a public tuning interface.
limits.behavior: I/O deadline and partial-evidence paths use shortened budgets; the production duration is source-inspected.

limits.title: Validator exit grace
limits.counting: Polling grace after closing validator pipes.
limits.effect: Expiry triggers a SIGKILL attempt, then reaping; failures remain reported.
limits.control: Production default; test-only controls are not a public tuning interface.
limits.behavior: Cleanup paths use controlled children; the production duration is source-inspected.

limits.title: Exec child deadline
limits.counting: Per-exec child observation deadline after successful spawn.
limits.effect: Worker attempts to kill/reap the child; the step records that the deadline fired.
limits.control: Production default; test-only controls are not a public tuning interface.
limits.behavior: Shortened deadline and cleanup controls; the production duration is source-inspected.

limits.title: Runner RPC wait
limits.counting: Client wait for the runner reply.
limits.effect: An expired wait yields runner_timeout; it does not expand the inner worker or validator budgets.
limits.control: Default; --timeout-ms changes only this wait and floors its value at 1 ms.
limits.behavior: The production wait and timeout response are source-inspected; compiled default agreement is tested.

limits.title: Validator query payload
limits.counting: Serialized JSON bytes for one probe, before the LF delimiter. Escaping counts. The 65536-byte fgets buffer reserves space for LF and NUL.
limits.effect: An overlong line produces one parse_error with no step ID; that prediction is unavailable. Later lines can still be processed.
limits.behavior: Exact payload boundary and over-limit drain/recovery controls in the native validator; overlong input also goes through the CLI.

limits.title: Controller subprocess output
limits.counting: Per stdout or stderr stream captured from the runner client, policy helper or log observer. Byte prefix before lossy text decoding; not an envelope-wide cap.
limits.effect: Output beyond the prefix is marked truncated. Truncated JSON stdout is not parsed as a complete reply.
limits.behavior: Exact prefix and truncation-boundary controls. Collection buffers the entire stream first; this is not a memory limit.

limits.title: Rejected validator frame context
limits.counting: Raw prefix of the first rejected frame, before base64 encoding.
limits.effect: The remaining frame is not retained as context; frame_bytes, retained_bytes and context_truncated describe the loss.
limits.behavior: Exact and over-limit invalid-frame context controls; no rejected bytes become verdicts.

limits.title: Exec child output per stream
limits.counting: Retained bytes in each stdout/stderr text buffer, excluding NUL. A truncation marker occupies part of this space on overflow.
limits.effect: Additional output is drained but not retained.
limits.behavior: Small stdout/stderr capture is tested. Overflow truncation and the exact retained-prefix/marker split are source-inspected.

limits.title: Primary worker diagnostic
limits.counting: Diagnostic payload bytes, excluding NUL.
limits.effect: The primary diagnostic is bounded and reports retained length and truncation state; it is not a transcript.
limits.behavior: Bounded diagnostic/truncation controls in the Swift worker evidence tests.

limits.title: Optional compiled-object capture
limits.counting: Raw bytecode bytes for a nonempty supported single-profile (type 0) object, before base64 encoding.
limits.effect: Oversize or unsupported objects leave capture unavailable without preventing policy application.
limits.behavior: Independently constructed object controls cover exact, excessive and unsupported captures.

limits.title: Worker observed path
limits.counting: Per-step C path-buffer payload bytes, excluding NUL.
limits.effect: Path observation can be absent or bounded; a host-side path diagnostic is a separate observation.
limits.behavior: Source-inspected buffer use; no exact path-length behavior claim is tested.

limits.title: Worker attempt error text
limits.counting: Per-step error-buffer payload bytes, excluding NUL.
limits.effect: Error prose is bounded; structured result/status fields remain separate.
limits.behavior: Source-inspected bounded formatting; no exact error-text boundary claim is tested.

limits.title: sbpl-check source admission
limits.counting: Top-level source bytes read by the diagnostic helper; not the runner policy cap.
limits.effect: policy_too_large without a compile verdict.
limits.behavior: Oversized input is tested through the shipped helper and fallback CLI; exact boundary behavior is source-inspected.

limits.title: sbpl-check import inventory depth
limits.counting: Top-level imports start at depth 0. At depth 8 the helper records a depth-limit diagnostic instead of reading/expanding that file.
limits.effect: Stops inventory expansion on that branch and marks imports_truncated. Does not impose this depth on libsandbox compilation.
limits.behavior: Deep import-chain control in the helper unit tests.

limits.title: sbpl-check import inventory count
limits.counting: Maximum records accumulated by the helper traversal, including unresolved/error records; visited files/names are deduplicated.
limits.effect: Stops further inventory traversal and marks imports_truncated. Does not impose this count on libsandbox compilation.
limits.behavior: Import-count exhaustion control in the helper unit tests.

limits.title: Log observer stream text
limits.counting: Streaming helper mode only (--duration or --follow): retained nonempty, non-prelude log lines with one LF per line. Only whole lines that fit are retained.
limits.effect: The first overflowing line sets log_truncated and stops text accumulation. Deny-event arrays and JSONL emission continue separately; this is not a memory or total-report cap. The normal CLI log-show path does not use this inner cap.
limits.control: Fixed byte cap; --no-log-capture disables normal CLI log collection, not this helper capability.
limits.behavior: Compiled value agreement is tested. Streaming accumulation and overflow behavior are source-inspected.
